content.title: About
content.content: Frozen blueberries are the berries of the highbush blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum) harvested at peak ripeness and quickly frozen to lock in flavor, aroma, and nutrients. They have a sweet‑tart taste, tender texture, and a vivid blue color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blueberries are rich in anthocyanins, the pigments that give them their deep blue hue and strong antioxidant activity.
Freezing within 24 hours of picking preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C and other phytonutrients.
Among berries, blueberries contain the highest amount of vitamin K.
In the United States, frozen blueberries are a common ingredient in smoothies, baked goods, and sauces.
There are more than 30 cultivated blueberry varieties, differing in size, sweetness, and storage life.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Flavonoids may improve night vision and reduce the risk of macular degeneration.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 57 kcal, making it suitable for weight management.

items.title: Source of vitamins K and B6
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting, while B6 supports protein metabolism.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to blueberries.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although low in calories, blueberries contain natural sugars, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: If berries are not properly washed before freezing, pesticide residues may remain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen blueberries can be added to smoothies, yogurt, oatmeal, baked goods, sauces, or simply thawed and eaten as a fresh‑like fruit. They do not need to be pre‑thawed for cooking; they soften quickly in hot dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen blueberries in an airtight bag or container at –18 °C. Once thawed, consume within 1–2 days and do not refreeze.
